or “Lead Bank”) on behalf of consortium of lenders (viz State Bank of India, Punjab National 
Bank, IIFCL, Bank of Baroda, Indian Overseas Bank  & Union Bank of India ) (“ Lenders”), is

("SCM”/ “SCM Bidding”) for transferring their stressed loan exposure (as detailed in Para 2 
below)(“Stressed Loan Exposure ”) on “All Cash” and/  or “Cash- Security Receipts ( “SRs”)” 
structure and is soliciting binding bids in the form of irrevocable offers from eligible  ARCs 
(“Permitted Entities” or “ Bidders”) in accordance with RBI/  Bank’s Policy on Transfer of 
Stressed Loan Exposures, in line with the regulatory guidelines and applicable laws.  
However, please note that the transfer of Stressed Loan Exposure will be subject to final

solely responsible for conducting due diligence at its own cost and employing its own 
resources and under no circumstances, any lender shall be deemed to have made any 
representation, whatsoever, in respect of the Stressed Loan Exposure.

a. The profile of the Bidder (promoter/ and promoter group, key managerial 
personnel, shareholders and shareholding pattern). However, it shall be the sole 
obligation of the Bidders to ensure that they are eligible for buying the Stressed 
Loan Exposure. 
b. RBI registration certificate/ other Regulatory Authorities Certificate as applicable. 
c. Certificate of Latest net-owned Funds/ net worth.

f. KYC of the Authorised Signatory (PAN/Passport for signature proof and Aadhaar for

8. Eligible Permitted Entities can participate on “All Cash” and/or “Cash- Security Receipts” (SRs) 
structure, minimum 15 :85 under Cash – SR structure or better Cash – SR structure and also 
submit unconditional and irrevocable guarantee from a Scheduled Commercial Bank (First

portion. (Note: - A Permitted Entity who is unable to provide the guarantee as detailed above

9. Cut-off date denotes the date upto which all realization/ recoveries made shall be 
retained by the lenders. The cut-off date in the instant case is June 30, 2024.  
 
10. The present process is run under Swiss Challenge Method where Lenders have a 
primary offer of INR 300.00 crore in hand at 15:85 Cash-cum-SR structure {Cash (INR 45 
crore): SR (INR 255 crore)} on Cash:SR::15:85 structure termed as “Base Bid” or “Anchor 
Bid” from a primary bidder ( “ Base Bidder” or “Anchor Bidder”) and invite bids from 
eligible Permitted Entities on comparable terms. The terms offered by the Base Bidder 
which are agreed by the Lenders are mentioned in Annexure-I. 
 
11. Swiss Challenge Bidding Process 
 
a. The minimum mark up over the Base Bid required for the challenger bid to be 
considered shall be minimum increase of INR 15.00 Crores or multiples thereof 
(which is well within the  percentage limits of markup provided under the 
applicable RBI Circular ) from the Base Bid. For this purpose, mark up shall be 
calculated as the difference between challenger bid and Base Bid. The minimum 
mark-up is kept at Rs. 15 Crores, on Cash/ Cash: SR  basis, as the case may be.  
The first bid for Cash/Cash - SR would be Reserve Price plus minimum markup   
b. If no challenger bid crossed the minimum mark -up specified in the invitation, 
the Base Bid becomes the winning bid, subject to final approval by competent 
authority of the respective Lenders. 
c. If challenger bid(s) crosses the minimum mark -up specified at point (a) above, 
the highest challenger bid becomes the challenger bid (“ Challenger Bid ”) and 
the challenger bidder will be considered as highest bidder (“ Challenger 
Bidder”). 
d. The Base Bidder who has provided the Base/ Anchor Bid would be invited to 
match the NPV (Net Present Value) of the Challenger Bid, if any (after 
discounting the offered SRs @ 1 Year MCLR rate of Lead Bank (Sate Bank of 
India) currently @ 8.95 % p.a. for 3 years). If the Base/ Anchor Bidder, either 
matches the Challenger Bid or bids higher than the Challenger Bid then such 
bid shall become the winning bid, else the Challenger Bidder shall become the 
winning bidder (the “Acquirer”/ “Successful Bidder”) 
e. Acceptance of the offer shall be at the sole discretion of the Lenders and shall 
be subject to approval of the competent authority of the respective Lenders. 
 
12. In case of any bid in the Cash – SR Structure, the bids would be evaluated  based on the 
following conditions: 
a. Minimum 15 – 85 under the Cash – SR Structure or better Cash – SR Structure. 
b. Minimum mark-up between challenger bid and Base Bid shall be 15.00 Crores as 
detailed above in point 11 (a). 
c. The offer received under Cash – SR Structure must provide an acceptable 
guarantee of First-Class Bank on SR portion for a period of five year from the SR 
issuance date.  (Note: - A Permitted Entity who is unable to provide the

guarantee as detailed above shall provide full cash for the SR portion.) 
d. SR portion will be discounted for a period of three years with 1 Year MCLR rate 
of lead Bank (SBI) currently @ 8.95 % p.a.  
e. For Cash - SR bids, the Discounted SR amount will be added to cash amount and 
this adjusted amount will be treated as cash equivalent for evaluation of bids. 
f. Upside sharing shall be applicable only on cash – SR structure. The minimum 
upside sharing would have to be given in 85:15 (or better) in favour of Lenders 
(SR Holders) and Bidder.  
g. No other terms of the Bidders to be inferior to the terms of the Base Bidder. 
 
13. Please note that any taxes, stamp duty, any other imposition that may be arising out of 
the transaction shall be payable by the Acquirer. 
 
14. Lenders reserve the right to declare account as fraud or No Fraud on a future  date even 
after assigning the Stressed Loan Exposure.
